newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - White bids fall sharply.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat - White bids fall sharply.

text.p: Bids for white wheat fell sharply on Thursday in reaction to a dearth of export demand and increased farmer selling, several cash merchants said.

"Last week Pakistan bought from Australia instead of us and since then, we really haven't had any business," a Portland cash source said. "Yesterday and today, the farmer starting selling their old crop. It was a thin market and it didn't take much selling to knock it down hard."
Bids were down 22 cents a bushel in Portland and 18 cents in other parts of Oregon. In contrast, MGE July white wheat futures were down only seven cents per bushel.

Dark northern spring wheat bids were mostly higher, in line with gains in MGE spring wheat. Several cash sources said concerns were mounting about persistent dry weather in northwest North Dakota and eastern Montana.
"They need rain pretty soon to get the crop going and they haven't been seeing it," one merchant said. "They've got a shot at some rain this weekend but it's pretty slim."
